answer.short: Construction with $DC=AB=8\text{ cm}$ and $DA=CB=5\text{ cm}$, forming a non-crossed quadrilateral.
answer.worked: Draw $DC=8\text{ cm}$. Choose $A$ above $DC$ on the circle with centre $D$ and radius $5\text{ cm}$. The circle with centre $A$ and radius $8\text{ cm}$ meets the circle with centre $C$ and radius $5\text{ cm}$ at the intended point $B$ above $DC$. Join $AB$, $BC$ and $DA$, retaining the construction arcs.

spec.description: One valid sample construction, retaining compass arcs and identifying the required side lengths.
spec.mathematics: D=(0,0), C=(8,0), A=(3,4), B=(11,4); opposite sides have lengths 8 cm and 5 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; the choice of A is an example.

answer.short: $AB=DC=8\text{ cm}$ and $AD=BC=5\text{ cm}$. Both pairs of opposite sides are equal, so $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.
answer.worked: $AB=8\text{ cm}$ because $B$ lies on the circle with centre $A$ and radius $8\text{ cm}$; also $DC=8\text{ cm}$. Similarly, $AD=BC=5\text{ cm}$ because these are radii of the circles with centres $D$ and $C$. A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides equal is a parallelogram.
